text:
Jordan: Quick question - my partner and I had a baby last week. Partner has employer coverage but is on unpaid parental leave for 8 weeks. Can I add the newborn to my Redwood coverage now, or do we need to wait until partner's coverage comes back? Also worried about retro premium/proration.
Lina (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: You can add the newborn as a dependent within 30 days as a QLE (birth). Typically we enroll on the date of birth but premium/proration depends on payroll cutoffs.
Jordan: Okay cool. If I add now and partner elects to keep their employer coverage, will Redwood be secondary? Any docs you need?
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/newborn-enrollment  lists proof of birth, other carrier ID for coordination, and timelines.
Sam (Benefits): Short answers: 1) Yes - if partner's employer plan remains active, that carrier will usually be primary. 2) We need the newborn's birth certificate (or hospital record) + partner's insurance card if that plan stays active. 3) We can set coverage effective retro to DOB if paperwork is submitted within 30 days.
Jordan: If I enroll now and later partner's coverage lapses while they're on leave, can I switch Redwood to primary? What about payroll deductions already taken?
Sam (Benefits): You can request a change (QLE) when partner drops coverage. We'll do COB (coordination of benefits) and update primary/secondary. Retro premium refunds: if Redwood becomes primary retroactively, we may issue retro claims adjustments and premium credits. But payroll can only correct so far back — Payroll handles refunds separately.
Raj (Payroll): FYI payroll window: premiums are deducted on the first payroll after benefits events are processed. If we owe a refund for premiums, we can issue a retro payroll credit, usually processed within the next 2 pay cycles after Benefits passes the case. Keep receipts.
Jordan: Got it. Timeline: I can upload docs to the portal?
Lina (People Ops): Yes - People Ops > Manage Dependents. Upload birth record + partner carrier card (front/back) and note "Jordan - newborn QLE". We'll tag Benefits and Payroll.
Jordan: One more: partner is on unpaid leave (no paycheck) so partner's employer coverage might show as active but not paying. Should I still enroll newborn to be safe?
Sam (Benefits): If partner's coverage might terminate while on leave, enrolling with Redwood now gives you immediate claim coverage (secondary if partner keeps theirs). That prevents gaps. If partner's plan terminates, file a QLE to change primary; we'll aim to minimize out-of-pocket.
Jordan: Uploaded hospital discharge + partner insurance screenshot. Thanks.
Lina (People Ops): Case created #BP-9256. Well confirm effective date (expect DOB retro if docs good) and notify payroll for any prorated refunds. :white_check_mark:
Jordan: Amazing, appreciate the quick help! :pray:
